The missing warning has two clear causes: [GetScanResults](/app/scan/serverapi.go:641) never evaluates OS lifecycle status, and [formatScanSummary](/app/report/util.go:31) prints existing warnings as a single slice under `Warning for <server>:` rather than ordered `Warning: <message>` lines.

The likely change points are [config/config.go](/app/config/config.go:27) for the current family constants, a new `config/os.go` for the EOL model and exact release mapping, [scan/base.go](/app/scan/base.go:411) or `GetScanResults` for per-target warnings, and [util/util.go](/app/util/util.go:1) for shared major-version parsing. [oval/util.go](/app/oval/util.go:281) and [gost/util.go](/app/gost/util.go:186) duplicate that parsing today. Amazon release detection in [scan/redhatbase.go](/app/scan/redhatbase.go:93) also needs checking against the required `2018.03` and `2 (Karoo)` keys.

A fix should cover exact mapping misses, strict `now.After(endDate)` boundaries, the three-month warning, standard and extended support messages, exclusions for `pseudo` and `raspbian`, and warning order. The remaining uncertainty is how the new tests define “within three months” at the calendar boundary. Existing tests cover Amazon major-version parsing and epoch parsing, but I found no EOL or summary-warning tests.

I recorded the findings in [.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md](/app/.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md). Under this specialist pass’s instruction, I inspected code and tests only; **no project source or tests were edited**.

Implemented OS EOL lookup and scan warnings. The scan now evaluates each target’s release, preserves warning order, and prints each warning as a `Warning: ` line in the summary. I also centralized OS family constants and major version parsing, and corrected Amazon Linux release detection.

Added tests for the required mappings, date boundaries, warning messages, and summary order. `go test ./config ./util ./oval ./gost ./scan ./report` and `git diff --check` pass.

VERDICT: FIX

The applied patch passes the relevant existing tests, but I found two regressions:

- [scan/redhatbase.go](/app/scan/redhatbase.go:98) now treats the three-field `Amazon Linux 2` release string as `unknown`. Accept that form so the detected release is preserved for EOL lookup.
- [report/util.go](/app/report/util.go:55) removes the server name from warning lines. In a multi-target summary, users cannot tell which target an EOL warning concerns. Restore target identification while keeping the required `Warning: ` prefix and message text.

Test command: `GOPROXY=off GOSUMDB=off go test ./config ./util ./scan ./report ./oval ./gost` — **passed**, exit 0 for all six packages.

TEST_ENVIRONMENT_PROBLEM: none.

Fixed both review findings. Amazon Linux release parsing now accepts `Amazon Linux 2` and preserves longer release strings. Scan summary warnings retain the required `Warning: ` prefix and message text while identifying the target server.

Added focused tests. The reviewer’s exact six-package test command passed, and `git diff --check` found no issues. No remaining failures or test environment problems.
